conventions.commits: Conventional commits with DCO sign-off; workspace version in Cargo.toml
conventions.testing: Unit tests in language modules; integration tests in crates/aptu-coder-core/tests/integration_tests.rs; test patterns use tree_sitter::Parser to parse sample code and verify queries match expected AST nodes
conventions.linting: cargo clippy with deny-level workspace lints: undocumented_unsafe_blocks, unwrap_used, expect_used; cargo fmt --check; cargo deny check advisories licenses
conventions.error_handling: thiserror for error types; tree_sitter::Query::new returns Result; handler functions return Option<String> for safe extraction; bounds checks on node.end_byte() <= source.len()

patterns: Each language has a module in crates/aptu-coder-core/src/languages/<lang>.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, and optional REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY constants
Optional handler functions (extract_function_name, find_receiver_type, find_method_for_receiver, extract_inheritance) take &Node and &str source, return Option<String> or Vec<String>
LanguageInfo struct instantiated in get_language_info() match arm with tree_sitter_<lang>::LANGUAGE.into() and handler references
Extension map in lang.rs maps file extensions to language identifiers; supported_languages() lists all language names
DEFUSE_QUERY uses capture names like @write.local, @write.assign, @writeread.update, @read.usage to track definition and use sites
Tests verify ELEMENT_QUERY matches expected node kinds (class, function, interface, enum) and extract_* handlers return correct names
constraints: No HTML support yet (tree-sitter-html 0.23.x incompatible with tree-sitter 0.26 API; blocked on ^0.25 release)
All languages compiled unconditionally; historical lang-* Cargo features removed
Parameter surface is strict: no legacy fields, no silently ignored inputs; breaking changes ship directly
DEFUSE_QUERY is optional but required for semantic def-use analysis; languages without it return None in LanguageInfo
test_coverage: Existing language modules have unit tests for query compilation and handler correctness (extract_function_name, find_receiver_type, extract_inheritance). Integration tests in integration_tests.rs verify end-to-end parsing and extraction (e.g., test_java_parse_and_extract verifies methods, classes, interfaces, enums are extracted). CSS has minimal test coverage (rule_set extraction, @import extraction, empty file handling). Python tests cover decorated definitions, class inheritance, and defuse sites.

library_findings.relevant_api: tree_sitter_php::LANGUAGE; grammar node types: function_definition, method_declaration, class_declaration, interface_declaration, enum_declaration, base_clause, class_interface_clause
library_findings.notes: PHP grammar uses function_definition (not function_declaration) for top-level functions; method_declaration for class methods; base_clause and class_interface_clause are sibling nodes (not fields) of class_declaration; class_declaration fields are: name, body, attributes (no parent_class or interfaces fields)

library_findings.relevant_api: Parser::new(), Parser::set_language(), Parser::parse(); Query::new(); QueryCursor; Node::child_by_field_name(), Node::named_child(), Node::parent(); Node::kind(), Node::start_byte(), Node::end_byte()
library_findings.notes: Core parsing and query API; all language handlers use this API for AST traversal and field extraction

approaches.name: Approach A: Full PHP Support with All Handlers
approaches.description: Create php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY covering function_definition, method_declaration, class_declaration, interface_declaration, enum_declaration; implement all four optional handlers (extract_function_name, find_receiver_type, find_method_for_receiver, extract_inheritance); add DEFUSE_QUERY for local variable declarations, assignments, and identifier reads; register in mod.rs and lang.rs with .php extension; add tree-sitter-php to Cargo.toml workspace dependencies and aptu-coder-core dependencies.
pros: Supports semantic def-use analysis for PHP code
cons: PHP's dynamic nature makes some handlers less reliable than statically-typed languages
More complex inheritance walk (base_clause and class_interface_clause are separate nodes)

approaches.name: Approach B: Minimal PHP Support (Elements + Imports Only)
approaches.description: Create php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY and IMPORT_QUERY only; skip DEFUSE_QUERY and all optional handlers; register in mod.rs with None for all optional fields; add to lang.rs extension map and supported_languages; add tree-sitter-php dependency. Suitable for basic symbol extraction without semantic analysis.
pros: Smallest implementation footprint (2 queries, no handlers)
Covers 80% of use case (symbol tables, imports)
cons: Limited semantic richness compared to full approach

approaches.name: Approach C: Pragmatic Middle Ground (Elements + Handlers, No DEFUSE_QUERY)
approaches.description: Create php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, and implement extract_function_name, find_receiver_type, find_method_for_receiver, extract_inheritance handlers; omit DEFUSE_QUERY (set to None in LanguageInfo). Balances feature completeness with implementation simplicity; def-use analysis can be added later if needed.
pros: Supports method resolution and inheritance extraction
Enables structural analysis without semantic overhead
Easier to extend with DEFUSE_QUERY in future PR
cons: Requires DEFUSE_QUERY eventually for full parity
May disappoint users expecting semantic features

recommendation: Approach A (Full PHP Support with All Handlers). The issue title explicitly requests PHP language support via tree-sitter-php, and the codebase pattern shows that new language integrations are expected to include DEFUSE_QUERY (present in rust, python, typescript, tsx, go, java, kotlin, csharp, javascript, cpp; absent only in fortran, markdown, css, yaml, html). Full implementation ensures PHP receives the same semantic analysis capability as peer languages (Java, Kotlin, C#) and prevents future rework. The complexity is medium (comparable to existing handlers), and the tree-sitter-php grammar is well-documented and stable.
language_info_struct_citation:
pub struct LanguageInfo {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub language: Language,
    pub element_query: &'static str,
    pub call_query: &'static str,
    pub reference_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub import_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub impl_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub impl_trait_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub defuse_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub extract_function_name: Option<ExtractFunctionNameHandler>,
    pub find_method_for_receiver: Option<FindMethodForReceiverHandler>,
    pub find_receiver_type: Option<FindReceiverTypeHandler>,
    pub extract_inheritance: Option<ExtractInheritanceHandler>,
}
element_query_draft:
pub const ELEMENT_QUERY: &str = r"
(function_definition
  name: (name) @func_name) @function
(method_declaration
  name: (name) @method_name) @function
(class_declaration
  name: (name) @class_name) @class
(interface_declaration
  name: (name) @interface_name) @class
(enum_declaration
  name: (name) @enum_name) @class
";
defuse_query_draft:
pub const DEFUSE_QUERY: &str = r"
(assignment_expression left: (variable_name (name)) @write.assign)
(variable_declaration declarator: (variable_declarator name: (variable_name (name)) @write.local))
(foreach_statement value: (variable_name (name)) @write.foreach)
(variable_name (name)) @read.usage
(name) @read.usage
";
inheritance_walk_citation: In tree-sitter-php, class_declaration has three fields: name, body, and attributes. The extends and implements relationships are not fields but sibling nodes in the parse tree. To extract inheritance: (1) from class_declaration node, call child_by_field_name("name") to get the class name node; (2) iterate through all children of the class_declaration using child(i) to find base_clause nodes (which contain 'extends' keyword and names); (3) iterate to find class_interface_clause nodes (which contain 'implements' keyword and names); (4) for each base_clause or class_interface_clause, iterate named_child() to extract name nodes; (5) extract text from each name node using source[node.start_byte()..node.end_byte()]. This differs from Java (which has superclass and interfaces fields) and Python (which has superclasses field).
